proposition.claim:
For all 0<sigma<2s0-1 there exists beta in (0,1) with 2s0 beta-1>(sigma+1)/2>sigma.

n=2,s=s0=3/5,sigma=1/10,Phi(t)=t,Lambda=1,u=0,mu=0,R=1 satisfy Lemma4.6 assumptions. This tests parameter existence, not failure of the zero solution.

The formal PV operator, displayed energy, and weak form use the same normalization.

Phi(t)=t, nonconstant u=psi smooth compact support, any n>=2,0<s<1; mu=(formal Lu)dx finite with locally bounded and integrable-tail density.

An averaged Sobolev norm is bounded by the unnormalized seminorm with c(n,gamma,q), no R factor.

n=2,q=2,gamma=1/2, g_R=x1/R on B_R; n>q gamma and finite seminorm.

At h=2s-1 the normalized comparison seminorm has RHS R^(-s/2+2s-n) times measure mass.

n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,u_R=R^(2s) phi(x/R) with nonzero C_c^infty(B_1/2) bump; v_R=0 since exterior values vanish; mu_R is its weak-form forcing, bounded in B_R.

The inhomogeneous difference-quotient Holder estimate has no R^(2s) multiplying its data term.

n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,beta=1,h=e1; phi smooth supported B1 and equal x1 on B1/2; w_L=L phi(x/L),R=L^2,L>3; f_L is the weak-form forcing. All energy/tail/bounded-forcing hypotheses and h<R/8 hold.

Truncated-to-classical Riesz comparison has c(n) for arbitrary beta in (0,n).

n=2, beta=2-epsilon with0<epsilon<1, unit Dirac measure at e1,x0=0,R=exp(1/epsilon).

A qth-power estimate is bounded by a qth root, and first differences divided by |h|^(1+gamma) have a finite global supremum.

For p.19 q=2, smooth cutoff H=G xi from g=x1^2 and arbitrary positive amplitude; all seminorms finite. For p.20 n=2,R=1,h0=1/10,gamma=1/2,g=x1 on required ball, with xi=1 on B21/20; (2.16) holds.
